g.text: Single-threaded 30-minute polling loop: watermark -> pull -> Parquet -> DuckDB upsert -> LanceDB -> watermark-commit
CREDENTIAL BOUNDARY — the RSA signing key lives on the shared `data` volume, which docker-compose.yml:269 also mounts into the orchestrator that executes LLM-generated SQL (secrets.py:50)
sync-worker — one container, ONE thread, ZERO async (Dockerfile:34 `python -m syncworker.main`, uid 10001)
Dashed red rectangle = trust boundary (credential material crossing a shared volume).
Red arrow = credential-bearing, externally-reachable or config-mutating hop.
Thick amber arrows 1 -> 5 -> 7 = the crash-safety ordering:
read watermark, land the data, THEN commit the watermark. Never the other way round.
Dotted purple rectangle = Python package grouping, not a process boundary.
Every arrow label is "what · protocol · sync|async · file:LINE".
Amber notes = retry / timeout / unbounded resource / swallowed exception, each anchored to a read file:LINE.
"blocking" is stated on every hop because this service has NO async code at all:
one thread, one cycle at a time, one object at a time (main.py:239-243).
